Pawan Kumar Chandana Is Taking India’s Private Space Industry to New Heights

The eyes of a nation were on the sleek, blue and white, 72-ft. tall Vikram-1 rocket when it zipped off its launchpad in Andhra Pradesh, India, on July 18, 2026, carrying half a dozen small satellites to low-Earth orbit 280 miles up. It was the first time the world’s most populous nation orbited a payload launched by a privately built and owned rocket, and Prime Minister Narenda Modi was making the most of it.
